dedupe_keys.name: meteoswiss hail climatology switzerland radar based spatial climate analyses

description: The MeteoSwiss hail climatology is a set of radar-derived grids for Switzerland: monthly and yearly maximum expected hailstone size (MESHS) and anomalies, numbers of hail days and of days with hail above 2 cm and 4 cm, a long-term hail-day climatology from 2002, and hazard return values of hailstone size for return periods of 2 to 100 years. It was developed by MeteoSwiss in a public-private partnership as a nationally uniform basis for hail risk assessment, using the HailStoRe resampling approach. Coverage is all of Switzerland on a 1 km grid, for the April to September hail season from 2002. Format and access: grid files downloadable from the federal STAC API and STAC Browser, with DOI 10.18751/Climate/Griddata/CHHC/1.0 and product documentation. Licence: MeteoSwiss Open Data, free and unrestricted with the source cited. Caveats: sizes and hail days are inferred from radar parameters, not measured on the ground, and radar coverage limits some Alpine valleys. It gives hail hazard inputs, including return periods, for hazard exposure and adaptation studies of buildings, grids, vehicles and crops. A related catalogue record is the NASA passive microwave hail climatology, which covers the globe at coarser resolution.
